attributions.claim: Girgis and colleagues described the cruciate anatomy from cadaveric dissection in the 1970s, including the bundle arrangement and the way tension shifts between bundles through flexion.
Noyes worked on the mechanical properties of the ligament itself in the same decade, including the effect of loading rate and of specimen age on failure load and failure pattern.

Butler, Noyes and Grood ran the sequential sectioning study that produced the primary and secondary restraint framework in the 1980s: load the knee, cut one structure, load it again, and attribute the difference.
Markolf measured in situ force in the ligament directly rather than inferring it from displacement, which made it possible to ask what a given surgical or rehabilitation manoeuvre actually loads.
Beynnon and Fleming took that question into living knees with implanted strain transducers, measuring ACL strain during the exercises patients were being given.
